result.title: A Scientific Claim Stability Framework for Evaluating MRI Morphometry Pipelines
result.comment: 44 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track)
result.summary: MRI morphometry pipelines are often evaluated by measurement agreement or downstream accuracy, yet their scientific value depends on the conclusions they support. Two pipelines can produce similar feature-level results yet support different conclusions about aging, cognitive decline, or neurodegeneration. We introduce Scientific Claim Stability (SCS), a claim-centric evaluation framework that converts region-of-interest (ROI) morphometry tables into auditable claim cards and evaluates their support under changes in dataset, processing pipeline, atlas, feature family, and target. Across 10,370 MRI scans from three datasets and five cohorts, SCS generates 2,783 claim cards and evaluates 89 claim-family pairs. The evaluation distinguishes stable, transferable, and fragile claims. FreeSurfer 8-FastSurfer comparisons show high evidence concordance and low anatomical-support overlap under the primary covariate specification. Acquisition-adjusted analyses show that the magnitude of support disagreement depends on the model specification. Structured review by specialists in geriatrics, neuroscience, and radiology, alongside auxiliary ChatGPT and Gemini reviewers, assesses claim plausibility, clarity, faithfulness, usefulness, and caution. SCS provides a reproducible way to audit the evidential stability of morphometry claims without assuming a universal gold standard.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Scientific Claim Stability（SCS）以「主张」为中心的评价框架，将 MRI 形态学 ROI 表转换为可审计的 claim card，并在数据集、处理流程、atlas、特征族与目标变化下检验主张支持度，区分稳定、可迁移与脆弱主张，并结合专家与 LLM 评审。
